resources.string: Opens Couch when you press Home.
Opened, but for under a minute
%1$s has no channel on this TV. Press OK to open it.
Screen time shows here once Couch has usage access. The setup guide shows how to turn it on.
OK to pick up an app · Back when done
Left or right to move it · OK to drop it
Pick a card. Automatic guesses from the input’s name.
Rows: apps, inputs and channels as rows of cards. Index: a list of your apps, with what the selected one has for you and how much you use it.
Small to see more apps at once, large to read from across the room.
The glow around the selected card and the progress bars.
Shows each app’s and input’s name under its card.
The synopsis of the selected film or episode, at the top of the screen.
Photo of the day: a new Bing photo every day.\nReddit: the best images of a subreddit, changing through the day.\nMy image: wallpaper.jpg, sent over ADB.
The subreddit used when the source is Reddit. Only TV-shaped images are kept.
How often the Reddit image changes.
The darker it is, the easier text is to read on a bright image.
Choose which rows show and in what order.
The name and icon of each HDMI input.
The rows your apps publish (Jellyfin, YouTube…). Turn on the ones you want to see.
Uncheck an app or input to hide it from the home screen.
Goes back home: OK to pick up an app, left or right to move it.
Current temperature and sky, next to the time. Data from Open-Meteo.
Leave empty to find it from your connection. The city found shows under the temperature.
After this long on the home screen without touching the remote: large clock, weather and wallpaper. Any button closes it.
This TV has no settings screen for this. The help on the right gives another way.
Opens Couch when you press HOME, on TVs that send HOME to their own launcher. Turn on “Couch: Home button” in the accessibility settings. Not needed if HOME already opens Couch.

Shows what’s playing in the top bar and, on Fire TV, the recommendations apps post. If the TV has no screen for it: adb shell cmd notification allow_listener cloud.samlo.couch/cloud.samlo.couch.MediaListener
Screen time in the Index layout and the Recent row. If the TV has no screen for it: adb shell appops set cloud.samlo.couch GET_USAGE_STATS allow
The preview channels apps publish (YouTube, Jellyfin and others). If the TV has no screen for it: adb shell pm grant cloud.samlo.couch android.permission.READ_TV_LISTINGS
"OK: show or hide · Long press: move"
"Up or down to move · OK to drop"
Check the rows to show on the home screen.
No channels yet. Apps publish them once you open them.
"OK: choose the icon · Long press: rename"
Pick the icon from cards, or long-press to rename the input.
Once a day, Couch asks GitHub for its latest release and shows an Update button left of the weather when there is one.
Version %1$s is available. Press OK to install it.
Couldn’t install the update. Try again later.
The download didn’t match its checksum, so it wasn’t installed.
This version is signed with a different key. Uninstall Couch, then install it.
Hidden tools for this TV: connect Couch to the TV’s debugging service, then remove the apps the TV came with.
What you change here affects the whole TV, not just Couch.

Android will ask “Allow USB debugging?” about a computer: that computer is Couch. Tick “Always allow”, then choose Allow, left of Cancel. If Couch can’t connect, turn on USB debugging in the developer options. Fire TV doesn’t allow this: use a computer.
Answer the question on the TV
Removes apps the TV came with, a few at a time, and keeps a list so you can put each one back. Only apps on Couch’s own list for this brand are offered.

Takes this page out of Customize, after putting back anything still running under it: TV settings, the home screen, the frame HUD and pre-releases. Removed apps are not: put them back from the list first if you want them.
Couch first asks the TV which apps are installed. Nothing is removed until you pick apps and confirm.
Lists the built-in apps Couch knows for this brand, grouped by how safe they are to remove, with what each one does.
Apps such as the home screen, WebView and Play services. Removing one can stop the TV from starting up, so Couch never touches them.
Couch removes 4 apps at a time. After each batch, restart the TV and check that it still works before going on. Removal keeps each app’s files so it can come back: it frees memory, not storage.
Removes each app for the TV’s user with pm uninstall -k --user 0. Its files stay on the TV, so it can be put back.
Before going on, check the TV: picture, sound, inputs and the home screen. If something is wrong, choose Undo this batch.
Puts this batch’s apps back and stops. Earlier batches stay removed.
Every app Couch removed. Choose one to put it back.
OK puts the app back with cmd package install-existing. Depending on the TV, its settings may be reset.
Puts back every app on this list, one after another. Any that fails is reported.
Back to the list of apps that can be removed.
The first reading is from the first scan, the second from now. Free memory changes from minute to minute, and a restart frees some on its own.
Apps Couch removed and hasn’t put back, and apps that were put back.
The list of removed apps stays available, even after a restart.
This TV doesn’t let apps use its debugging service (Fire TV blocks it). Run the commands below from a computer instead.
Type this on a computer on the same network as the TV.
Couch checks which apps are really gone and adds them to the list of removed apps.
The question on the TV wasn’t answered in time. Try again with the TV awake.
Couch couldn’t reach the TV’s debugging service. Turn on USB debugging in the developer options, then try again.
Removes the apps of this batch. Android may ask “Allow USB debugging?” first: tick “Always allow”, then choose Allow.
Ends the batches. Apps already removed stay on the list of removed apps.
Some TVs bring removed apps back when they start. Restart, then come back here: Couch picks up where you stopped.
Couldn’t restart from here. Restart from the TV’s settings, then come back.
Checks that each app of this batch is still gone. If any came back, OK removes them again.
This TV doesn’t let Couch put apps back. Run these from a computer, after adb connect and adb shell.
Puts this app back when run in adb shell on a computer.
Couch checks which apps are back and takes them off the list.
Ads, promotions and shopping on the TV’s screens. Nothing else depends on it.
Sends usage or viewing data to the maker, or tracks you for ads. Nothing on screen depends on it.
Store demo mode, demo content or first-setup tutorials.
Settings for hotels and shops. Not used at home.
Help, manuals, bug reports and logs for the maker’s support.
One of the maker’s own apps: a media player, store, browser or games. Remove it if you don’t use it.
Interactive features of broadcast TV. Remove it if you only stream.
Extra voice-assistant features. The assistant itself stays.
The stock screen saver. Couch’s ambient mode can take its place.
A Google app you may not use. It can be reinstalled later.
Reads the screen aloud for people who can’t see it. Keep it if anyone in the home needs it.
A built-in feature most people don’t use. Remove it only if you know you don’t need it.
Only used during the TV’s first setup, or to register it.
Installs partner apps without asking, usually after setup.
Lets phones cast or mirror to the TV. Remove it only if you never do; Chromecast stays.
Nothing here is weighing on this TV
None of the built-in apps Couch knows runs all the time or uses memory right now, so removing them wouldn’t change how the TV feels.
These apps aren’t running, so removing them frees nothing. They’re here if you want them gone anyway.
Not running now; starts for a moment when the TV turns on.
Not running: removing it frees nothing on this TV.
Lets phones cast or mirror to the TV. Removing it ends that.
Plays music, photos and videos from USB or a media server.
Voice search and the remote’s mic button rely on it.
Reads the screen aloud. Keep it for anyone who needs it.
Brings the TV’s software and security updates.
Other features rely on it, such as casting, the remote’s app buttons or a TV tuner.
Your account sign-in or the TV’s network setup depends on it.
Part of the TV’s own home screen.
Guides disagree on whether removing it is safe, so Couch leaves it alone.
You opened it on %1$s. Couch doesn’t offer apps you use.
Clears every app’s cache. Apps rebuild what they need as they go, so it’s safe, and on a full TV it frees far more space than removing built-in apps.
This TV doesn’t let Couch do it. On a computer: adb shell pm trim-caches 999G
Puts back every TV setting godmode changed (animation speed, ad blocking), exactly as it was before. Removed apps have their own list.
Your TV is back as it was.
Couch needs the TV’s debugging service for this. Connecting…
How fast Android’s windows and transitions move. Off makes every screen appear at once, 0.5× halves the wait.
Android’s private DNS for the whole TV. AdGuard’s free server blocks the ads and trackers most apps load, but not the ads inside YouTube videos. Android’s default only encrypts lookups.
The hostname of a private DNS server you run or trust, such as a Pi-hole or NextDNS address. Setting it switches ad blocking to it.
Closes apps left running in the background, as Android would when memory runs low. They open again normally.
Also offers Couch’s test versions when they come out. Couch never goes back to an older version, even if you turn this off.

A small panel on the home screen: one line per remote press with its slowest frame, and what slowed it down when it ran over budget. Milliseconds show the headroom a fast frame has; frames a second never claims more than the screen can show. It only redraws after you stop pressing, so it never measures itself.
Goes back to the home screen and plays the same set of presses every time, then shows the frame times. Press any key on the remote to stop it.
This TV won’t let Couch connect by itself

On the TV: Settings › Device preferences › About, press Build seven times, then turn on USB or network debugging in Developer options. On a computer on the same network, install Android’s platform-tools and run the two commands below. This page notices the grant by itself.

%1$s
It lets Couch change the TV-wide settings on this page. It lasts until Couch is uninstalled, and “Put my TV back” undoes every change.
Permission received. The settings are unlocked.
Puts the TV on standby after this long, even if you leave Couch.
Waits ten seconds, so you can go to the screen you want, then saves it to Pictures.
The TV took the screenshot itself; look in its Screenshots folder.

HOME opens Couch directly, without the accessibility workaround, by making Couch Android’s preferred home. Nothing is turned off, and uninstalling Couch hands HOME back by itself. Some TVs ignore the preference; they keep working through the workaround. “Put my TV back” or OK here undoes it.
HOME is back to how it was.
Couldn’t hand HOME back yet. Try again; if it keeps failing, choose the home in the TV’s settings.
Couch is now the TV’s home.
This TV kept its own home. Nothing changed; HOME still opens Couch through the accessibility workaround.
Share screen time with the other TVs in the house, over your home network only. Nothing goes through the internet.
Screen time only, per app. It is encrypted and goes straight between your TVs.
Lets the TVs you pair see how long each app was used here, and shows you theirs. Off by default; turning it off stops all of it.
In Index, either this TV alone or every paired TV added together. Apps match by package, or by name when the package differs.
What your other TVs call this one.
Press OK twice to forget this TV. It stops sharing right away, and its screen time leaves your totals.
Open this on both TVs, then pick the other one here. Both screens show the same six digits; one OK on each confirms.
Open Add a TV on the other TV too
Pair with this TV. Both screens will show six digits to compare.
If the other TV doesn’t show up, type its address, as it appears in its network settings.
The other TV must show these same six digits.
Press this only if both screens show the same digits.
Cancel the pairing. If the digits really differ, someone else on your network may be in the way.
Couldn’t reach that TV. Open Add a TV on it too.
